writeup: TIC 264163792 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry with an orbital period of 1.2937 days. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 1.64 percent, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal shows strong statistical significance with a box least-squares detection value of 726.0. Pixel-level analysis using difference imaging confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 28.9, though the centroid offset of 4.1 arcsec warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be previously unknown. The machine learning screening model assigns it a score of 0.73, indicating reasonable confidence in its validity as a real target.
